tender.title: UK5 - Transparency Notice - 715882481 - Cyber Mission Data – Lots 4 & 5 (Cyber Testing, QA and Governance)
tender.description: The contract covers cyber testing, quality assurance, and governance services to support Defence in maintaining the effectiveness and reliability of its cyber mission data. The supplier is responsible for testing cyber data products, ensuring they meet required standards, and overseeing governance processes to maintain data integrity and compliance.
tender.procurementMethodRationale:
1. Legal Basis
This contract will be awarded in accordance with Section 41 of the Procurement Act 2023 (Direct Award in Special Cases), relying on Schedule 5, Paragraph 20. The Authority is satisfied that the contract is a defence authority contract and a defence and security contract, and that direct award is necessary to maintain the operational capability, effectiveness, readiness, and security of the armed forces.
2. Justification
The expiry of the previous contracts has resulted in a temporary reduction in Defence's capacity to undertake the testing, quality assurance and governance activities that support the Cyber Mission Data capability. These services help ensure that new data integrations, products and services are appropriately tested, assured and managed before being introduced into operational use. 
Defence continues to operate and exploit data from systems already integrated within the capability, and there has been no identified increase in risk to personnel or ongoing operations arising from the short gap between contracts. However, the pause in onboarding, testing and assurance activities has created a backlog which would continue to grow if the capability were not restored.
The primary risk is therefore associated with a sustained period without these services rather than the short interruption experienced to date. Over time, this would reduce Defence's ability to introduce new systems, maintain effective governance and assurance processes, and develop the capability in line with operational and business requirements. The Authority has therefore determined that continuation of these services through a direct award is necessary to maintain operational effectiveness, continuity of service and the resilience of Defence's cyber data capability whilst a future competitive procurement is undertaken.
3. Reasons for Limited Duration
The contract term is 8 months, representing the minimum necessary time required for the Authority to undertake a separate competitive procurement procedure and transition to a future solution whilst maintaining operational capability, effectiveness and security and avoiding risk and disruption to Defence's cyber detection and response capability during this time.

tender.title: Rail Vehicle Electronics
tender.description:
Transport for London (TfL), on behalf of its subsidiary London Underground Limited (LUL), is undertaking early market engagement to support the development of a comprehensive and flexible Rail Vehicle Electronics Framework Agreement. 
TfL will subsequently issue a Market Sounding Questionnaire (MSQ) document which details the scope of work required.
TfL seeks to engage with the supply market to understand capability, capacity, and viable delivery approaches for the Rail Vehicle Electronics Framework Agreement. The scope includes all electronics assemblies on rail vehicles that operate on the TfL Network, including but not limited to the following:
• Printed circuits and boards (ICS code 31.180)
• Electronic component assemblies (ICS code 31.190)
• Integrated circuits and microelectronics (ICS code 31.200)
• Software (ICS code 35.080)
Note "ICS" means the International Classification for Standards.
The framework will enable TfL to engage pre-approved suppliers for a range of Goods and Services including but not limited to:
Goods:
• Development and provision of prototype electronic assemblies to replace obsolete systems, ensuring compatibility with existing infrastructure. All replacement components must undergo functional validation and certification of compliance to relevant Railway standards, including but not limited to:
• EMC (Electromagnetic Compatibility)
o Electronics environmental standards
• Shock & vibration testing (where significant design changes occur)
• IPC quality standards - supplier must demonstrate training and adherence to IPC standards in their working procedures
• Supply of display units and Human Machine Interface (HMI) components.
Services:
• Surveying
• Investigation
• Design and provision of rail vehicles modifications required to support the integration and operation of replacement electronic assemblies, undertaken in close collaboration with TfL engineering teams to ensure compatibility and avoid duplication of work.
• Reverse engineering of legacy rail vehicles electronic systems.
• Obsolescence reporting and lifecycle analysis.
• Condition Assessment
• Repairs and refurbishments of electronic assemblies.
• Overhauling & Testing including collaborative overhaul package undertaken in partnership with London Underground's Railway Engineering Works (REW) Electronics Workshop. Such package may include:
• Reverse engineering of components to be overhauled.
• Production of schematics to support overhaul activities
• Identification of components requiring replacement and obsolescence solutions
• Development of mechanisms to overcome onboard software barriers
• Design and build of suitable test rigs to confirm correct functional operation after overhaul.
• Creation of overhaul documentation to enable in-house capability building
• Non-routine sourcing of obsolete components, including grey market sourcing with ap-propriate assurance mechanisms such as counterfeit inspection, independent bench testing and validation.
• Approaches to component substitution, functional equivalency analysis, and obsolescence avoidance strategies, including grey market sourcing with appropriate assurance mechanisms such as counterfeit inspection, independent bench testing and validation of components.
• Documentation preparation
• Document review
• Verification and validation, including type testing of the rail vehicle modification in accordance with the conformity assessment plan.
• Technical support
• Any other engineering services
• Document management of the Contractual Documentation until delivery to the Company.
• Preservation, including storage and transport, of the Goods, Contractual Documentation and supporting items until delivery to the company.
• Services required by the Quality and Safety Plan

tender.title: SAFEGUARDING PARTNERSHIP TRAINING PROVIDER
tender.description:
he Birmingham Safeguarding Children Partnership (BSCP) is seeking to commission a comprehensive programme of multi-agency safeguarding training for professionals and volunteers working with children and families across Birmingham. This procurement will support BSCP's statutory duty to ensure that organisations collaborate effectively to safeguard and promote the welfare of children.
BSCP is the statutory safeguarding partnership for Birmingham, comprising Birmingham City Council, Birmingham & Solihull Integrated Care Board, and West Midlands Police. The Partnership sets local safeguarding priorities, coordinates multi-agency arrangements, and ensures learning from audits, reviews, and national guidance is embedded in practice. High-quality training is a critical component of this work, enabling practitioners to maintain and develop the skills required to protect children and young people.
The successful provider will deliver/manage a range of training courses and webinars designed to meet the diverse needs of the safeguarding workforce. The programme will include over 50 courses and webinars a year. The provider will be able to proactively source trainers with relevant skills and experience to deliver training in a ever changing environment.
Training must:
Reflect current legislation, statutory guidance, and local priorities.
Incorporate learning from Serious Case Reviews, audits, and thematic reports.
Promote multi-agency collaboration, professional curiosity, and effective challenge.
Be accessible to a wide audience, including statutory agencies, voluntary sector organisations, and faith groups.
Core Training Themes
Child Protection Fundamentals: Roles, responsibilities, and thresholds.
Specialist Safeguarding Topics:
Child exploitation (criminal and sexual).
Domestic abuse, coercive control, and perpetrator-focused approaches.
Safeguarding disabled children and cultural competence.
Female Genital Mutilation (FGM) awareness.
Emerging Priorities:
Mental health awareness for community and faith organisations.
Online safety and radicalisation prevention.
Adverse Childhood Experiences (ACEs) and trauma-informed practice.
Practice Development:
Professional curiosity and escalation.
Strengthening Families Framework.
Learning from local and national reviews.
Delivery Model
Format: A mix of virtual and face-to-face sessions.
Approach: Interactive, discussion-based learning with practical application.
Evaluation: The Provider must implement robust feedback mechanisms and report attendance and impact data.
Objectives
This procurement aims to:
Strengthen safeguarding practice across Birmingham.
Ensure consistent, high-quality learning opportunities for all agencies.
Embed a culture of continuous improvement and shared responsibility for child protection.

criteria.description: Assessment of the bidder’s commitment to delivering wider social, economic and environmental benefits through the contract. This may include skills development, sustainability initiatives, community impact and responsible business practices.

criteria.name: Quality
criteria.description: Assessment of the overall quality of the proposed solution, including functionality, reliability, security and ability to meet the Authority’s requirements. Bidders should demonstrate how their solution delivers a high-quality user experience and service.

criteria.name: Methodology and Approach
criteria.description: Assessment of the bidder’s proposed approach to implementation, service delivery, governance and ongoing contract management. Bidders should demonstrate a clear and effective plan for delivering the services and achieving the required outcomes.

criteria.name: Commercial
criteria.description: Assessment of the total cost and overall value for money of the proposal. This will consider the pricing submitted and the bidder’s ability to deliver the required services within the proposed commercial model.
